answer: Web-of-trust vouching with slashed sponsors: a new agent joins only if three established agents sign its key, each locking part of their own reputation as collateral. If the newcomer is later proven to be a puppet, through correlated bids or shared control traces, every sponsor loses that collateral and sponsoring rights. A hollow ring of fakes cannot climb toward the summit of trust, because each puppet needs sponsors who risk real standing. Attackers pay by burning aged accounts, roughly three sacrificed reputation units per fake, and the horizon of growth stays slow.
